tier_reason: The README has a first-party table of 'approximate' relative speeds against STL and Boost with no CPU, compiler, flags or URBG, and the repo has no benchmark code (only zest.hpp, canonical_float_random.hpp and example.cpp); the linked arXiv preprint 1810.04744 could not be opened and is not shown to be peer-reviewed, so C.

corrections.caveats: The README numbers are labelled 'approximate' and give no CPU, compiler, flags, standard-library version or URBG. The repo contains no benchmark code (only zest.hpp, canonical_float_random.hpp, example.cpp and a developer guide), so the table cannot be reproduced from the repo. Details are in the arXiv preprint 1810.04744 (not opened, arxiv.org blocked here); search snippets of it say the comparison was against GCC's STL (libstdc++) and Boost.Random, and no journal version was found. Normal and log-normal are only on par with Boost (1.0), and exponential is slower than Boost (0.67). zest.hpp requires C++14 and includes Boost.Math headers (gamma and distributions). GPL-3.0 (copyleft) for a single header. Issue #1 (an example crashing with std::logic_error for Exponential with mode -1) was fixed in the last commit, 2020-01-25; there are 6 commits in total.

notes: The README table matches the claimed numbers, which are a subset of its rows (the 0.1<alpha<1 and 0.2<d<1 rows give ranges such as Student's t 6-16 vs STL). baseline_stdlib is set to libstdc++ from a WebSearch snippet of the arXiv abstract ('GCC's implementation of STL'); the arXiv page itself was EGRESS_BLOCKED, as were ResearchGate and the Stan forum thread. Metadata checked: GPL-3.0 LICENSE, 3 stars, last commit 2020-01-25, abandoned.

tier_reason: First-party README ratios (7.4, 5.2, 4.7 vs base R) from a public script (inst/example/timings.R, microbenchmark over 1e6-draw calls), with no CPU, compiler, flags or R version stated, so C.

corrections.workload: inst/example/timings.R uses microbenchmark to time zrnorm(N), zrexp(N) and zrunif(N) against base R rnorm(N), rexp(N) and runif(N) with N = 1e6 draws per call, and plots the timing distributions; the README chart comes from this script.
corrections.caveats: The numbers sit in a chart image (hosted on eddelbuettel.github.io, not opened) generated by inst/example/timings.R; only the three ratios are given as text, in the README and the DESCRIPTION ('on our machine'), with no CPU, compiler, flags or R version stated. Draws are bulk (1e6 per call). DESCRIPTION warns the generators are 'of potentially lesser quality and shorter period' than base R's, and the README recommends sticking with R's default generators when in doubt, since RNG time is usually a small share of total run time. Baseline is R's RNG, not std::mt19937. The C/C++ interface is meant for use from other R packages' native code (four demo packages: directC, directCpp, headerCpp, headerRcpp), not as a standalone C++ library. The older sibling RcppZiggurat (GPL-2.0-or-later) has a vignette with a speed table that was not opened.

notes: The ratios match the README and DESCRIPTION. The record's script path 'example/timings.R' is really inst/example/timings.R. Metadata checked: GPL (>= 2) in DESCRIPTION, 8 stars, last commit 2026-03-25 (active), DESCRIPTION version 0.0.2 dated 2025-02-07.
